name: UFWS World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Filled on the federation's opening night, 22 April 1991, by a twelve-man tournament whose final also decided the North American belt: the winner took the world title, the loser the second. Sargent Sledge Hammer won it and held it for seven weeks, and the record's last word is that he holds it still. Between those two facts it changed hands five times in ten weeks, once when a whole stable beat the champion unconscious behind the referee's back.
notes: Declared in the federation's own recruitment announcement of 8 April 1991 — “The PWGA World Champion, who will defend against the No.1 Contender each week” — and filled by tournament on 22 April (promotions/ufws/archive/pwga-by-e-mail-1991-04-08.html, promotions/ufws/archive/pwgea-report-1-1991-04-22.html). One reign begins inside the unheld Report #11 and is chained across that gap at month precision.

name: UFWS North American Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The federation's second singles belt, and the only one filled by losing: the runner-up in the opening night's World title tournament took it as a consolation. Its own announcement said the champion would defend against any of the top five contenders, chosen by the president himself so that different people got shots — and it changed hands seven times in four months, including once at the Summit of E-Wrestling and once inside an issue that does not survive.
notes: Declared in the federation's own recruitment announcement of 8 April 1991 — “the PWGA North American champ, who will defend against any one of the top 5 contenders (I will make the choice myself, so as to give different people title shots)” — and filled on 22 April by the tournament final's losing side. One change happened at the Summit of E-Wrestling (its own wing, id `summit-of-e-wrestling`) and one inside the unheld Report #11; both are chained at month precision with the reason given on the reign.

name: UFWS World Tag-Team Championship
epitaph: Filled by a six-team tournament on the opening night and defended almost every week after it. Seven reigns in four months, two of them by the same team twice over, and the belts finished the record on the team that lost the very first final.
notes: Declared in the federation's own recruitment announcement of 8 April 1991 — “the PWGA Tag-Team champions, who will defend against the No.1 contenders” — and filled by tournament on 22 April. One reign begins inside the unheld Report #11 and is chained across that gap at month precision.

name: UFWS All-Jobber (Junior Heavyweight) Championship
epitaph: A championship for the bottom of the card, restricted by the federation's own rules to wrestlers built on 145 power points or fewer, and the first belt it ever awarded — Baron Von Klaw won the All-Jobber final before either of the other tournaments reached its own. It changed hands seven times, was held for one week by a man who was North American Champion at the same time, and ended the record on a Soviet technician the standings had classed a jobber all summer.
notes: Declared in the federation's own recruitment announcement of 8 April 1991 — “the PWGA All-Jobber champion, a title restricted to wrestlers with 145 power points or less (not counting the 25 free power points for class moves)” — and filled by a six-man tournament on 22 April. The belt is called both the All-Jobber and the Junior Heavyweight title in the federation's own text, sometimes in the same issue. One reign begins inside the unheld Report #11 and is chained across that gap at month precision.

name: UFWS North American Tag-Team Championship
epitaph: The federation's fifth and last championship, announced in July 1991 alongside the founding of the All-Jobber Confederation and filled by a nine-team tournament whose final closed the second SuperCard. The New Mystics won it and were still champions three days later, when the record ends.
notes: Announced in the federation's own Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and filled at the second SuperCard on 26 August 1991 (promotions/ufws/archive/ufws-supercard-2-1991-08-26.html). The federation's own text is the authority and it says five.
